Title:
Cilium agent fails to start with bpf file system mounted on the host

Description:
Followed the instructions to install the Cilium etcd operator here: https://cilium.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gettingstarted/k8s-install-etcd-operator/ The instructions recommend mounting the bpf file system on the host. But with this, the agent fails to start. Logs from the cilium pod show this error message: ``` level=fatal msg="Unable to mount BPF filesystem" error="multiple mount points detected at /sys/fs/bpf" subsys=bpf ``` **General Information** - Cilium version - 1.4 - Kernel version (run `uname -a`) - 4.15 - Orchestration system version in use 1.13 and 1.12 Seen the same behaviour with docker as well as cri-o.

If yes please use the exact version available in https://github.com/cilium/cilium/tree/master/examples/kubernetes where they are different depending on each k8s version. For example, since k8s 1.11 the cilium DaemonSet for crio does not have the volumes for bpf directories set in the container. Let me know if that is the issue.

Title:
Quick Install - Fails mounting BPF crio due to multiple mount points

Description:
**General Information** - Cilium version (run `cilium version`) - v1.6.90 - Kernel version (run `uname -a`) - 5.2.7-816.native - Orchestration system version in use (e.g. `kubectl version`, Mesos, ...) - v1.15.2 - Link to relevant artifacts (policies, deployments scripts, ...) - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cilium/cilium/master/install/kubernetes/quick-install.yaml - Upload a system dump (run `curl -sLO releases.cilium.io/tools/cluster-diagnosis.zip && python cluster-diagnosis.zip sysdump` and then attach the generated zip file) **How to reproduce the issue** 1. Paso 1 - kubeadm init on master running on Clear Linux using crio 2. Paso 2 - kubectl apply -f https://.../quick-install.yaml 3. Paso 3 - Get the following error on the cilium pods: ``` level=info msg="Cilium 1.6.90 a96d7f4fe 2019-08-06T11:32:30-07:00 go version go1.12.7 linux/amd64" subsys=daemon level=info msg="cilium-envoy version: 2e42144f26667ddee9f5d2506019f16c57386b29/1.11.0-dev/Modified/RELEASE/BoringSSL" subsys=daemon level=info msg="clang (7.0.0) and kernel (5.2.7) versions: OK!" subsys=daemon level=info msg="linking environment: OK!" subsys=daemon level=info msg="bpf_requirements check: OK!" subsys=daemon level=info msg="Detected mounted BPF filesystem at /sys/fs/bpf" subsys=bpf level=fatal msg="Unable to mount BPF filesystem" error="multiple mount points detected at /sys/fs/bpf" subsys=bpf ``` FYI - Deploying the old way works every time: kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cilium/cilium/1.6-backports-19-07-25/examples/kubernetes/1.15/cilium-crio.yaml From a quick look it seems that the crio specific deployment doesn't mount /sys/fs/bpf which looks to be the main issue. Cheers

Title:
[Win10] - Folders do not mount successfully when drive K: already exists.

Description:
My desktop has had a K drive for almost as long as I can remember... which, as I discovered, the keybase client apparently does not like. My kbfs logs are full of lines like the following: ``` [ERRO kbfs mounter.go:57] 01f Failed to mount dokan filesystem (i=8): Dokan failed: code=-5 "Mount error" [ERRO kbfs mounter.go:57] 02a Failed to mount dokan filesystem (i=16): Dokan failed: code=-5 "Mount error" [ERRO kbfs mounter.go:57] 02b Failed to mount dokan filesystem (i=32): Dokan failed: code=-5 "Mount error" [ERRO kbfs mounter.go:57] 02c Failed to mount dokan filesystem (i=64): Dokan failed: code=-5 "Mount error" [ERRO kbfs mounter.go:57] 02d Failed to mount dokan filesystem (i=128): Dokan failed: code=-5 "Mount error" ``` Upon investigation, I found that the "mountdir" setting in config.json doesn't appear to do anything... changing it from "K:" to an unused letter didn't force keybase to use it. Changing my K drive to a different letter seems to be a suitable workaround, albeit an inconvenient one. Please let me know if more information would be helpful.

Comments:
- You can change the kbfs drive letter by running `keybase kbfsmount set X:` on the keybase shell and then restarting. https://github.com/keybase/client/issues/4317#issuecomment-260665549
- Thank you for linking to that other ticket... I did search before creating a new one, but didn't find anything.

Installing OCP 4.7 on baremetal with IPI installation. When the control plain node boot from PXE in legacy mode, the kernel going to panic state with the error : No filesystem could mount root, tried: Kernel panic - not syncing: VFS: Unable to mount root fs on unknown-block(0,0) The bootstrap machine is on Vmware VM. This is the autogenerated IPXE on httpd pod: :retry_boot echo In inspector.ipxe imgfree kernel --timeout 60000 http://172.20.20.60:80/images/ironic-python-agent.kernel ipa-inspection-callback-url=http://172.20.20.60:5050/v1/continue ipa-inspection-collectors=default,extra-hardware,logs systemd.journald.forward_to_console=yes BOOTIF=${mac} ipa-debug=1 ipa-inspection-dhcp-all-interfaces=1 ipa-collect-lldp=1 ipa-api-url=http://172.20.20.60:6385 initrd=ironic-python-agent.initramfs || goto retry_boot initrd --timeout 60000 http://172.20.20.60:80/images/ironic-python-agent.initramfs || goto retry_boot # What you expected to happen? The control plain node boot, and cluster gone up. # How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? It always happens. I tried with OCP 4.6 and OCP 4.7. In install-config.yaml i have the setting bootMode: legacy. ```console $ ./openshift-baremetal-install --dir ~/clusterconfigs --log-level debug create cluster ``` # Anything else we need to know? Retrying the installation several times, sometimes I get: uncompression error - system halted! # References <!-- Are there any other GitHub issues (open or closed) or Pull Requests that should be linked here? For example: - #6017 --> - Similar to https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1952167. But in this case it is working in legacy mode.

- Cool - I'll take a closer look when I get a chance this week. But let me jot some thoughts to provide some context first: CircleCI builds use lxc containers actually and we rely on nested lxc support (i.e. lxc-in-lxc) for docker support. LXC should work also "out-of-the-box". We also run on unprivileged lxc containers, where root-in-container != root-on-host, and we apply further apparmor restrictions to make the system secure, and restricting mknod operations. That may clash with privileged container starting, if it mounts /dev device files (e.g. /dev/null) with mknod. The suggested solution is to use bind-mounts when running in unprivileged-containers instead. In ordinary circumstances, lxc detects it's running on unprivileged container and does the right thing by using bind-mounts. If vagrant-lxc uses a custom lxc config files (or it imports a privileged-container config file), the lxc mount settings will need to be tweaked to use bind-mount. In our containers, the settings are: ``` lxc.mount.entry = /dev/console dev/console none bind,create=file 0 0 lxc.mount.entry = /dev/full dev/full none bind,create=file 0 0 lxc.mount.entry = /dev/null dev/null none bind,create=file 0 0 lxc.mount.entry = /dev/random dev/random none bind,create=file 0 0 lxc.mount.entry = /dev/tty dev/tty none bind,create=file 0 0 lxc.mount.entry = /dev/urandom dev/urandom none bind,create=file 0 0 lxc.mount.entry = /dev/zero dev/zero none bind,create=file 0 0 ``` I will dig a bit further during the week. Would love to have vagrant-lxc support :).

I have this working! :grinning: Ubuntu Trusty running on CircleCI (Ubuntu Precise) via vagrant-lxc All scripts/files are available at https://gist.github.com/username_3/36c75555683ac9db2309 ### Changes to `lxc-config`: * Remove the active AppArmor profile * Get rid of all the `cgroup.devices.allow` stuff in the default config * Add config from @username_2 above * Add extra mounts from https://github.com/lxc/lxc/issues/344#issuecomment-85040482 otherwise upstart hangs part way through waiting for the network to come up. ### Changes to `lxc-template` The point here was to avoid `tar` trying to make device nodes (`mknod` doesn't work in the Circle environment). There might be a better way (maybe at box creation time?), these happened to be the only device nodes in my rootfs. ```diff - (cd ${LXC_ROOTFS} && tar xfz ${LXC_TARBALL} --strip-components=${LXC_STRIP_COMPONENTS}) + (cd ${LXC_ROOTFS} && tar xfz ${LXC_TARBALL} --strip-components=${LXC_STRIP_COMPONENTS} \ + --exclude=./rootfs/dev --exclude=./rootfs/var/spool/postfix/dev) ``` ### Building a box I use the `vagrant-lxc-package.sh` script, since `vagrant package` seemed to ignore the extra-files options. Essentially the script just replaces `lxc-config` & `lxc-template` with my modified files. ### Next Would be nice to make this easier, so there's no need to replace the template & config file - any ideas @username_1?
